revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Festival Tickets
revealWordProblem.text:
Four friends are doing yard work around town to earn money for the Summer Music Festival advertised on the flyer. Tickets are $75.50 each. They charge $15 per hour for yard work and will combine their earnings.
Question: How many hours do the four friends need to work to earn enough money to buy four tickets? Propose a breakdown of how many hours each friend might work.
revealWordProblem.imageAlt: A Summer Music Festival flyer for August 5th and 6th at River Park Arena, priced at $75.50 per ticket.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: Four tickets cost 4 × $75.50 = $302. Let h be the friends' combined paid work hours at $15 per hour. The inequality is 15h ≥ 302, so h ≥ 302/15 = 20 2/15 hours, or 20 hours 8 minutes. Fractional hours are allowed unless the jobs require whole-hour billing. If they share the work equally, each needs 5 hours 2 minutes. If they choose whole hours, 21 combined hours earns $315; one workable split is 5, 5, 5, and 6 hours, leaving $13 after buying the tickets.

questions.stem: Which inequality represents: 'The temperature is less than 40 degrees'?
questions.explanation: 'Less than' means <, so the inequality is t < 40.
choiceFeedback: Your symbol opens toward temperatures ABOVE 40. 'Less than 40' lives on the other side — which way should the symbol point?
The ≤ symbol lets the temperature be exactly 40. 'Less than 40' leaves 40 out.
An equals sign pins the temperature to a single value, but this situation describes a whole range of temperatures.
hints: Find the comparison phrase: 'less than 40 degrees'. Does 40 itself count, or only temperatures below it?
'Less than' with no 'or equal to' means a strict symbol — no bar underneath — pointing toward the smaller side.
Test a value: is 35 degrees 'less than 40'? Yes — so pick the strict symbol that puts t on the smaller side of 40.
questions.stemEs: ¿Qué desigualdad representa: 'La temperatura es menor que 40 grados'?
questions.explanationEs: 'Menor que' significa <, así que la desigualdad es t < 40.
hintsEs: Halla la frase de comparación: 'menos de 40 grados'. ¿Cuenta el 40 mismo o solo las temperaturas por debajo?
'Menos que' sin 'o igual a' significa un símbolo estricto —sin barra debajo— apuntando hacia el lado menor.
Prueba un valor: ¿35 grados es 'menos de 40'? Sí, así que elige el símbolo estricto que pone t del lado menor de 40.

questions.stem: Which inequality represents: 'You must be at least 48 inches tall to ride'?
questions.explanation: 'At least' means greater than or equal to, so h ≥ 48.
choiceFeedback: So close — test the boundary. Does a rider who is EXACTLY 48 inches tall get to ride? Your strict symbol turns that rider away.
This describes riders who are too short to ride. Check which direction the symbol opens.
This would let anyone shorter than 48 inches ride. 'At least 48' makes 48 the smallest allowed height, not the largest.
hints: 'At least 48' — ask yourself: can a rider who is EXACTLY 48 inches tall ride? That decides whether 48 is included.
When the boundary value is allowed, you need a symbol with the 'or equal to' bar under it.
Allowed heights are 48, 49, 50, and up. Pick the symbol that includes 48 itself AND points toward bigger numbers.
questions.stemEs: ¿Qué desigualdad representa: 'Debes medir al menos 48 pulgadas de estatura para subir'?
questions.explanationEs: 'Al menos' significa mayor que o igual a, así que h ≥ 48.
hintsEs: 'Al menos 48': pregúntate si alguien que mide EXACTAMENTE 48 pulgadas puede subir. Eso decide si el 48 se incluye.
Cuando el valor del límite sí se permite, necesitas un símbolo con la barra de 'o igual a' debajo.
Las estaturas permitidas son 48, 49, 50 y más. Elige el símbolo que incluya el 48 Y apunte hacia los números mayores.

questions.stem: Which inequality represents: 'A store can hold no more than 75 people'?
questions.explanation: 'No more than' means less than or equal to, so p ≤ 75.
choiceFeedback: Almost — check the boundary. Is a store holding EXACTLY 75 people breaking the rule? Your symbol says yes; re-read 'no more than.'
This says the store always holds 75 or more people, which is the opposite of a limit. 'No more than' caps the number.
This describes crowds larger than the limit. 'No more than 75' means the store never goes above 75.
hints: 'No more than 75' — could the store hold exactly 75 people? Could it hold 76?
'No more than' allows the boundary but nothing above it — that calls for a symbol with the 'or equal' bar.
Test values: 75 people is fine, 76 is not. Pick the symbol that keeps p at 75 or below.
questions.stemEs: ¿Qué desigualdad representa: 'Una tienda puede albergar no más de 75 personas'?
questions.explanationEs: 'No más de' significa menor que o igual a, así que p ≤ 75.
hintsEs: 'No más de 75': ¿podría la tienda tener exactamente 75 personas? ¿Podría tener 76?
'No más de' permite el límite pero nada por encima: eso pide un símbolo con la barra de 'o igual'.
Prueba valores: 75 personas está bien, 76 no. Elige el símbolo que mantenga p en 75 o menos.

steps: 1. 'At least', 'minimum', 'no less than' translate to ≥ (greater than or equal to)
2. 'At most', 'maximum', 'no more than' translate to ≤ (less than or equal to)
reviewHighlights.watchOut: A common mistake in Write Inequalities is using a strict symbol (> or <) for a phrase that actually includes the boundary value. For 'the suspect is at least 18 years old,' students often write a > 18 instead of the correct a ≥ 18 — this wrongly excludes 18 itself, even though 'at least 18' means 18 counts as a match. The same error happens in reverse with 'at most': for 'the getaway bag holds at most 12 items,' students write n < 12 instead of n ≤ 12. Always ask: does the key phrase include the number ('at least,' 'at most,' 'no more than,' 'no fewer than' → use ≥ or ≤) or exclude it ('more than,' 'fewer than' → use > or <)?

level2.explanationEs: Halla la palabra clave: máximo 1,500 → 1,500 o menos Escribe la desigualdad: w ≤ 1,500

level2.stem: A parking lot has fewer than 40 empty spaces. Which inequality shows the number of empty spaces s?

hints: Does "fewer than" mean less or more? Is 40 included?
hintsEs: ¿«Menos de» significa menor o mayor? ¿Está incluido el 40?
level2.explanation: Find the key words: fewer than 40 → less, not 40 Write the inequality: s < 40
level2.explanationEs: Halla las palabras clave: menos de 40 → menor, no el 40 Escribe la desigualdad: s < 40
choiceFeedback: ≤ includes 40. But 40 spaces is not fewer than 40.
"Fewer than" means less, so the values go down from 40.
≥ means 40 or more. "Fewer than 40" means less than 40.

level3.stem: A fair ride requires each rider to be at least 48 inches tall. Let h be a rider's height in inches. Which inequality represents the heights that are allowed to ride?
choiceFeedback: This shuts out a rider who is exactly 48 inches tall. 'At least' includes the 48.
This admits only riders 48 inches and SHORTER. Taller riders are allowed too.
This admits only riders under 48 inches, which is the opposite of the rule.
level3.explanation: The phrase 'at least 48 inches' means 48 inches is allowed and any greater height is allowed too. That is greater than or equal to, so the inequality is h ≥ 48.

level3.stem: Clue: "The suspect is not taller than 70 inches." Which symbol goes in the box for the height h: h ☐ 70?
level3.stemEs: Pista: «El sospechoso no mide más de 70 pulgadas.» ¿Qué símbolo va en el recuadro para la estatura h: h ☐ 70?
hints: Could the suspect be exactly 70 inches tall? Could he be 72?
hintsEs: ¿El sospechoso podría medir exactamente 70 pulgadas? ¿Podría medir 72?
level3.explanation: Test the boundary number: 70 → not taller than 70 ✓ Pick the symbol that includes 70: h ≤ 70
level3.explanationEs: Prueba el número límite: 70 → no mide más de 70 ✓ Elige el símbolo que incluye el 70: h ≤ 70

level3.stem: A pool is open to swimmers no younger than 7. Which symbol goes in the box for a swimmer's age a: a ☐ 7?

hintsEs: ¿Puede nadar un niño de 7 años? ¿Uno de 6? ¿Uno de 10?
level3.explanation: Test the boundary number: 7 → not younger than 7 ✓ Pick the symbol that includes 7: a ≥ 7
level3.explanationEs: Prueba el número límite: 7 → no es menor de 7 ✓ Elige el símbolo que incluye el 7: a ≥ 7

level3.stem: A bridge sign says: "Trucks over 12 tons may not cross." Which inequality shows the weight w of a truck that may cross?
level3.stemEs: Un letrero de un puente dice: «Los camiones de más de 12 toneladas no pueden cruzar.» ¿Qué desigualdad muestra el peso w de un camión que sí puede cruzar?
hints: The sign names the trucks that cannot cross. Which trucks can? Can a 12-ton truck?
hintsEs: El letrero nombra los camiones que no pueden cruzar. ¿Cuáles sí pueden? ¿Puede uno de 12 toneladas?
level3.explanation: Test the boundary number: 12 tons → not over 12 → may cross Write the inequality: w ≤ 12
level3.explanationEs: Prueba el número límite: 12 toneladas → no pasa de 12 → puede cruzar Escribe la desigualdad: w ≤ 12
choiceFeedback: A truck of exactly 12 tons is not over 12, so it may cross. < leaves out 12.
That shows the trucks that may NOT cross.
That includes trucks over 12 tons, and they may not cross.

level3.stem: A number n is at least 4 and less than 9. How many whole numbers can n be?
level3.stemEs: Un número n es al menos 4 y menor que 9. ¿Cuántos números enteros puede ser n?
hints: Write both inequalities. Is 4 included? Is 9 included?
hintsEs: Escribe las dos desigualdades. ¿Está incluido el 4? ¿Está incluido el 9?
level3.explanation: Write both inequalities: n ≥ 4; n < 9 List the whole numbers that fit both: 4, 5, 6, 7, 8 Count them: 5 numbers
level3.explanationEs: Escribe las dos desigualdades: n ≥ 4; n < 9 Haz una lista de los enteros que cumplen las dos: 4, 5, 6, 7, 8 Cuéntalos: 5 números

tool.instructions: Each graph shows one real-world rule. Write the inequality that matches the circle and the shading.

problems.label: The temperature is less than 40 degrees
You must be at least 48 inches tall to ride

hints: Open circle → the boundary is NOT included, so the symbol is < or >. Closed circle → the boundary IS included, so the symbol is ≤ or ≥.
Shaded to the right means the values are greater ( > or ≥ ). Shaded to the left means the values are less ( < or ≤ ).
'At least' means the boundary counts, so use ≥. 'More than' means it does not, so use >.

workedSteps.answer: They need at least 20 2/15 hours (20 h 8 min) — about 5 h 2 min each. With whole hours, 21 hours split 5, 5, 5, 6 earns $315 and leaves $13.
